the_question: The head probe earlier today found 14 of 14 obvious destinations had demand, which establishes that the 74-city evidence set is a sample rather than the head. It says nothing about how far down the tail the demand runs, and the arithmetic for this axis turns entirely on that. A projection off a head sample would have been a guess dressed as a number.
how_the_sample_was_chosen: By TOURISM POI from the rebuilt aggregation, not by population. Population is explicitly the wrong instrument here and this project already paid to learn it: Szklarska Poreba has 6,970 people and 9,300 searches a month. A population-ranked tail of destination countries is mostly industrial cities and district towns no traveller searches, so it would have returned near zero and been read as a dead tail when it had really measured the wrong thing. A first attempt using raw POI city tags was also discarded: it reached only 28 cities, because most POI carry no city tag and are attributed spatially, and that spatial attribution had never run over a destination country until the 2026-10-06 rebuild. Cities already carrying entity-level evidence were excluded, leaving 120 uncovered destination cities with a tourism list page, and the sample was spread across ranks 25 to 400 of that list.

the_finding_that_matters_most: TOURISM POI COUNT DOES NOT PREDICT DEMAND. The sample was ordered by tourism POI descending and the volumes ignore that ordering completely: Luzern 36 POI and 1,800 searches, Olten 27 POI and 20 searches, Fatima 21 POI and 40 searches, Tavira 9 POI and 350 searches, Laufen 8 POI and zero. The correlation is weak enough to be useless as a gate. So tourism POI is a decent instrument for FINDING candidate destinations, which is what it was used for here, and worthless for deciding which of them deserves a page. Demand has to be measured per city. There is no proxy, and any build that infers demand from a count of things on a map will produce pages for Laufen.

what_it_means_for_scale.candidate_pool: 120 uncovered destination cities currently hold a tourism list page in the rebuilt aggregation
what_it_means_for_scale.if_the_52_percent_hit_rate_holds: about 63 of them would carry 100 or more monthly searches in at least one licensed language
what_it_means_for_scale.why_that_is_not_a_page_count: each viable city then multiplies by the languages its country licenses, between one and four, and by the destination-capable families, and then every gate applies. The localisation gate alone removed 122,106 rows on the last run.
what_it_means_for_scale.and_why_the_pool_itself_will_grow: 120 is what eleven captured destination countries yield. The queue is still running, and India alone holds 1,285 destination cities that already pass the language-evidence test and lack only the OSM layer.
what_it_means_for_scale.honest_order_of_magnitude: low thousands of pages on this axis, not the hundreds of thousands the 1,000,000 target needs. Worth building, and not the answer.

the_cheapest_next_measurement: The same 21-city probe in en and ja, the other two widely licensed languages across these countries, to see whether the 52 percent hit rate is a property of the cities or of German. About 950 units.
